statement: Among tumor-classified spots, those that are immediately neighbored by immune-classified spots (defined purely from the 'Classification' annotation and a fixed 6-nearest-neighbor graph in spatial coordinates) exhibit higher interferon-response, antigen-presentation, and immune-checkpoint program scores than tumor-classified spots that lack immune-classified neighbors.
biological_rationale: In breast tumors, lymphocyte-rich niches frequently develop at invasive margins where T cells and other immune cells contact tumor cells, triggering interferon signaling, antigen presentation, and upregulation of immune checkpoints in nearby tumor cells. The exploration log documents immune gene-expression hotspots at tumor–stroma interfaces (e.g. OBSERVATION_001, OBSERVATION_003, OBSERVATION_011), and CellVoyager summaries (CV1) highlight tumor–immune boundaries as potentially important microenvironments. To avoid circularity, this hypothesis defines immune adjacency strictly from the histology-derived 'Classification' labels and a fixed k-nearest-neighbor graph, without using interferon or checkpoint expression to construct the groups. If localized immune–tumor crosstalk is a major driver of tumor immune activation, tumor spots with immune-classified neighbors should systematically show stronger interferon, antigen-presentation, and checkpoint programs even after adjusting for local sequencing depth and array-edge effects.

data_subsets.base_filter: Load library/datasets/dataset.h5ad. Restrict to spots with obs['in_tissue'] == True (if available) and non-missing obsm['spatial']. Exclude spots whose obs['Classification'] is in ['Artifact', 'Empty', 'Background', 'NA'] or is missing.
data_subsets.tumor_spots: Define tumor-classified index spots as those with obs['Classification'] in ['Invasive cancer + lymphocytes', 'DCIS'] (restricting to categories present in the dataset).
data_subsets.immune_neighbor_spots: Define immune-classified neighbor spots as those with obs['Classification'] in ['Lymphocytes', 'Normal + stroma + lymphocytes'] (i.e. lymphocyte-enriched classes derived from annotation, not from interferon/immune gene expression). These spots are NOT used as index tumor spots in this analysis.
data_subsets.adjacency_definition: Construct a 6-nearest-neighbor (k=6) graph over all in-tissue, non-artifact spots using Euclidean distance in obsm['spatial'] (native pixel coordinates); do not impose an additional radius threshold. For each tumor index spot, label it 'immune-adjacent' if at least one of its 6 neighbors is an immune-classified neighbor spot; otherwise label it 'immune-distant'.
data_subsets.qc_filters: Within tumor index spots, exclude those with total_counts or n_genes_by_counts below the 10th percentile (computed over tumor spots only). For all retained tumor spots, store covariates log1p(total_counts), log1p(n_genes_by_counts), and distance_to_array_edge, where distance_to_array_edge is approximated as min(x - x_min, x_max - x, y - y_min, y_max - y) using obsm['spatial'] coordinates (x, y).

metrics: Module score per tumor spot for an interferon-response program, using an externally curated gene set (e.g. MSigDB Hallmark interferon-alpha and interferon-gamma response) intersected with genes present in the dataset.
Module score per tumor spot for an antigen-presentation program, constructed from curated MHC class I and II genes and related antigen-processing genes, restricted to genes detected in this dataset.
Module score per tumor spot for an immune-checkpoint program, using a predefined list of canonical checkpoint genes (e.g. PDCD1, CD274, CTLA4, LAG3, TIGIT and close analogs that are present).
For each program, summary statistics (mean, median, variance) of module scores in immune-adjacent versus immune-distant tumor spots, and effect sizes (e.g. difference in adjusted means or Cohen's d).
For each tumor spot, the count of immune-classified neighbors among its 6 nearest neighbors, and the correlation between this neighbor-count and each module score (after QC adjustment).
statistics: Primary: For each program module score, fit a linear model over tumor spots of the form module_score ~ immune_adjacent (binary) + log1p(total_counts) + log1p(n_genes_by_counts) + distance_to_array_edge, optionally adding x and y spatial coordinates as additional covariates. Test whether the coefficient of immune_adjacent is significantly positive.

As a non-parametric sensitivity analysis, compare module score distributions between immune-adjacent and immune-distant tumor spots using a Wilcoxon rank-sum test stratified or matched on total_counts quantiles to mitigate QC confounding.

Spatial permutation test: among tumor index spots, randomly permute the immune_adjacent versus immune_distant labels (keeping spatial coordinates and covariates fixed), recompute the difference in mean module scores between groups for each permutation (e.g. 1,000 permutations), and estimate an empirical p-value for the observed difference.

Neighbor-count association: test the (partial) association between the number of immune neighbors and each module score using linear regression including the same QC covariates, or Spearman rank correlation adjusted by regression residuals.
test_plan.multiple_testing: Control the false discovery rate across all primary program-level tests (interferon, antigen presentation, immune checkpoint) and any additional gene-level tests using the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure. Report both raw and FDR-adjusted p-values, with primary interpretation at an FDR threshold (e.g. 5%).
test_plan.expected_direction: Tumor spots labeled as immune-adjacent should have significantly higher interferon-response, antigen-presentation, and immune-checkpoint module scores than immune-distant tumor spots after QC adjustment, and module scores should increase with the number of immune-classified neighbors. Under spatial permutation of the adjacency labels, the observed group differences should lie in the extreme upper tail of the null distribution.

narrowing_notes: Tumor spots with immune-classified neighbors did not show significantly higher interferon, antigen-presentation, or checkpoint module scores after QC and covariate adjustment; effect sizes were small and permutation and Wilcoxon tests were non-significant after FDR, so localized immune adjacency is not a major determinant of these programs in this dataset.

statement: Within tumor-classified regions, epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT)/invasion program scores decrease with increasing distance from non-tumor tissue, while proliferation and cell-cycle program scores increase with distance, such that these programs exhibit opposing monotonic spatial gradients as a function of distance from non-tumor spots.
biological_rationale: Solid tumors often display radial organization, with more proliferative cells in central regions where nutrients and mechanical constraints may favor growth, and more invasive, EMT-like cells at the tumor–stroma interface where cells contact non-tumor matrix and vasculature. The exploration log notes differences between tumor core and edge (OBSERVATION_002, OBSERVATION_004, OBSERVATION_012), including invasion-related markers at boundaries and more proliferative markers centrally, and CellVoyager summaries (CV2) point to possible radial structure of tumor programs. To avoid circularity, this hypothesis operationalizes distance from non-tumor tissue directly from the 'Classification' labels and spatial coordinates, and uses externally curated EMT and proliferation gene sets, rather than selecting genes based on these same gradients. If edge cells preferentially engage EMT/invasion while core cells prioritize proliferation, EMT and proliferation scores should show opposite signed associations with distance to the nearest non-tumor spot.

data_subsets.base_filter: Load library/datasets/dataset.h5ad and restrict to spots with obs['in_tissue'] == True (if available) and valid obsm['spatial']. Exclude obs['Classification'] in ['Artifact', 'Empty', 'Background', 'NA'].
data_subsets.tumor_spots: Define tumor-classified spots as those with obs['Classification'] in ['Invasive cancer + lymphocytes', 'DCIS'], restricted to categories actually present.
data_subsets.non_tumor_spots: Define non-tumor spots as those with obs['Classification'] in ['Normal epithelium', 'Stroma', 'Stroma + adipose tissue', 'Normal + stroma + lymphocytes', 'Adipose'] (again restricted to labels available in the dataset).
data_subsets.distance_definition: For each tumor-classified spot, compute the minimum Euclidean distance in obsm['spatial'] to any non-tumor spot. Use these distances measured in the native pixel units as a continuous distance_to_nontumor variable. As a secondary discretization, define three groups by tertiles of distance_to_nontumor among tumor spots: 'edge' (lowest tertile), 'intermediate' (middle tertile), and 'core' (highest tertile), ensuring each group contains sufficient spots.
data_subsets.qc_filters: Within tumor spots, exclude those with total_counts or n_genes_by_counts below the 10th percentile among tumor spots. For all retained tumor spots, record log1p(total_counts), log1p(n_genes_by_counts), and spatial coordinates (x, y) from obsm['spatial'], as well as distance_to_array_edge computed as min(x - x_min, x_max - x, y - y_min, y_max - y).

metrics: Module score per tumor spot for an EMT/invasion program using an externally curated EMT gene set (e.g. MSigDB Hallmark EMT) intersected with expressed genes.

Module score per tumor spot for proliferation and cell-cycle programs, using curated gene sets such as MSigDB Hallmark G2M checkpoint and Hallmark E2F targets, each scored separately and/or combined into a single proliferation index.
For each program, Spearman correlation between module score and continuous distance_to_nontumor, and summaries of module scores within edge, intermediate, and core distance tertile groups.
Spatial maps of EMT and proliferation module scores overlaid on spatial coordinates for qualitative inspection that gradients align with tumor geometry.
statistics: Primary: For each module (EMT, G2M, E2F), fit linear regression models over tumor spots of the form module_score ~ distance_to_nontumor + log1p(total_counts) + log1p(n_genes_by_counts) + x + y, and test whether the distance_to_nontumor coefficient is negative for EMT and positive for proliferation programs.

Compute Spearman rank correlations between distance_to_nontumor and each module score; as a sensitivity analysis, compute Spearman correlations on residuals obtained after regressing module scores on the QC covariates (total_counts and n_genes_by_counts).

Discrete group comparison: perform Kruskal–Wallis tests for differences in EMT and proliferation module scores across edge, intermediate, and core groups. If significant, perform post hoc Wilcoxon rank-sum tests comparing edge vs core groups for each program, with effect sizes.

Optionally fit generalized additive models (GAMs) with smooth terms for distance_to_nontumor and spatial coordinates to confirm that the observed gradients are not solely due to a single spatial axis and to capture potential non-linear trends.
test_plan.multiple_testing: Apply Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction within families of related tests: one FDR correction across all EMT-associated tests, and another across all proliferation-associated tests (e.g. G2M and E2F modules), including both regression and correlation p-values when interpreting a given program. Report raw and FDR-adjusted p-values.
test_plan.expected_direction: EMT/invasion module scores should be significantly higher in tumor spots closer to non-tumor tissue (edge tertile) and decrease with increasing distance_to_nontumor (negative regression and correlation coefficients), whereas proliferation and cell-cycle module scores should be lowest near the edge and increase toward the core (positive coefficients). Opposing gradient directions for EMT and proliferation after QC and spatial adjustment would support the hypothesis.

narrowing_notes: Distance-to-non-tumor gradients were strong and highly significant: EMT module scores increased with greater distance from non-tumor tissue, while proliferation (G2M/E2F) scores decreased with distance and were highest at the tumor edge. This supports opposing spatial gradients but in the opposite direction from the pre-registered expectation (edge more EMT-like, core more proliferative), suggesting that the tumor in this sample has a proliferative rim and more mesenchymal core; the hypothesis should be refined to allow tumor- and sample-specific gradient orientations.

statement: Stromal spots that are immediately adjacent to tumor-classified regions (peritumoral stroma), defined from the 'Classification' labels and a fixed 6-nearest-neighbor graph, exhibit higher cancer-associated fibroblast and extracellular matrix (ECM)-remodeling program scores than stromal spots located farther from tumor regions (distant stroma).
biological_rationale: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) in peritumoral stroma are known to secrete and remodel extracellular matrix, often forming ECM-rich rims around invasive tumors. The exploration log notes stromal regions with strong ECM and fibroblast-like signatures near tumor borders (OBSERVATION_005, OBSERVATION_006, OBSERVATION_013), and CellVoyager summaries (CV3) highlight stromal heterogeneity consistent with localized CAF niches. To reduce circularity, this hypothesis defines peritumoral versus distant stroma solely from annotated 'Classification' labels and spatial adjacency, and uses externally curated ECM/CAF gene sets rather than selecting ECM genes from the same dataset. If CAF activation is spatially focused at the tumor margin, stromal spots abutting tumor should show systematically higher CAF/ECM program scores than stromal spots farther away, even after accounting for sequencing depth and array position.

data_subsets.base_filter: Load library/datasets/dataset.h5ad and restrict to spots with obs['in_tissue'] == True (if available) and valid obsm['spatial']. Exclude obs['Classification'] in ['Artifact', 'Empty', 'Background', 'NA'].
data_subsets.tumor_spots: Define tumor-classified spots as those with obs['Classification'] in ['Invasive cancer + lymphocytes', 'DCIS'], restricted to present labels.
data_subsets.stromal_spots: Define stromal spots as those with obs['Classification'] in ['Stroma', 'Stroma + adipose tissue']. Exclude 'Lymphocytes' and 'Normal + stroma + lymphocytes' to avoid mixing strong immune signatures into the CAF/ECM analysis.
data_subsets.adjacency_and_groups: Construct a 6-nearest-neighbor (k=6) graph over all in-tissue, non-artifact spots using Euclidean distance in obsm['spatial']. For each stromal spot, check its 6 nearest neighbors: if at least one neighbor is tumor-classified, label the stromal spot as 'peritumoral stroma'; otherwise label it as a candidate 'distant stroma' spot. Among candidate distant stroma, further require that the minimum Euclidean distance to any tumor spot exceeds the 75th percentile of stromal-to-tumor distances, to ensure these spots are truly far from tumor boundaries.
data_subsets.qc_filters: Within stromal spots, exclude those with total_counts or n_genes_by_counts below the 10th percentile among stromal spots. For all retained stromal spots, record log1p(total_counts), log1p(n_genes_by_counts), spatial coordinates (x, y), and distance_to_array_edge defined as min(x - x_min, x_max - x, y - y_min, y_max - y) from obsm['spatial'].

metrics: Module score per stromal spot for ECM-remodeling programs using curated extracellular matrix gene sets such as NABA ECM or related signatures, intersected with genes detected in this dataset.
Module score per stromal spot for CAF-like activation signatures derived from published CAF gene sets, restricted to present genes.
Summary statistics (mean, median, variance) and effect sizes for ECM and CAF module scores in peritumoral versus distant stromal spots.

Secondary: global Moran's I for ECM/CAF module scores across all stromal spots using the 6-nearest-neighbor graph, and local Moran's I (or similar local indicators of spatial association) to identify ECM 'hotspot' stromal spots.
statistics: Primary: For each ECM/CAF module score, fit linear regression models over stromal spots of the form module_score ~ peritumoral (binary) + log1p(total_counts) + log1p(n_genes_by_counts) + distance_to_array_edge, optionally including x and y coordinates, and test whether the peritumoral coefficient is significantly positive.

As a non-parametric sensitivity analysis, compare ECM/CAF module score distributions between peritumoral and distant stroma using Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, optionally stratified by total_counts quantiles.

Secondary spatial structure: compute global Moran's I for each ECM/CAF module score over stromal spots using the 6-nearest-neighbor graph and assess significance via permutation of module scores over the fixed graph. Compute local Moran's I to identify ECM hotspots, and test via permutation or enrichment analysis whether hotspot stromal spots are closer to tumor-classified spots (smaller minimum distance) than non-hotspot stromal spots.
test_plan.multiple_testing: When evaluating multiple ECM/CAF modules and individual genes, apply Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction across all primary group-comparison tests for these modules. Spatial autocorrelation tests (global and local) for multiple modules should be treated as a separate family with their own FDR control. Report raw and FDR-adjusted p-values.
test_plan.expected_direction: Peritumoral stromal spots should exhibit significantly higher CAF/ECM module scores than distant stromal spots after QC and edge adjustment. ECM/CAF module scores are additionally expected to show positive spatial autocorrelation among stromal spots, with identified ECM hotspots occurring preferentially near tumor boundaries, but the core hypothesis is the peritumoral > distant stroma contrast in ECM/CAF activity.

narrowing_notes: CAF/ECM module scores were strongly and significantly *lower* in peritumoral stromal spots than in distant stroma after adjusting for QC and array-edge covariates, with moderate-to-large negative effect sizes, while global Moran's I indicated robust spatial clustering of ECM/CAF activity. This contradicts the simple peritumoral > distant stroma expectation and instead points to ECM-rich niches in more distal stromal regions; the hypothesis should be refined to focus on non-monotonic or region-specific ECM patterns rather than a uniform peritumoral enrichment.
